prompt: House prices are reported as the middle price, so a few mansions don't distort the picture.
why: A few mansions would drag an average up, but the middle price barely moves. The median resists extreme values.
trap: The mansions are outliers; the measure that resists them is the median.

prompt: Line the five test scores up from lowest to highest and take the third one.
why: Sorting five scores and taking the third leaves two below and two above it. The middle of sorted values is the median.

prompt: A report on typical income uses the value with half of people above it and half below.
tells: half of people above it and half below
why: A value with half of people above it and half below is the definition of the median.
trap: The mean can sit far from the middle person.

prompt: Wait times are mostly 2 minutes with a few 60-minute waits, so the team reports the middle value instead of the average.
tells: reports the middle value instead of the average
why: A few 60-minute waits would pull the average far above the usual 2 minutes. The middle value shows the typical wait: the median.
trap: The data is skewed, but the measure picked is the median.

prompt: With an even number of values, take the two in the middle and use the value halfway between them.
tells: take the two in the middle
why: With an even count there's no single middle value, so you take the two middle ones and average them. That's how the median is defined for even counts.
trap: It isn't the mean of all values.

prompt: App ratings are sorted, and the one in the center is shown as typical.
why: Sorting the ratings and taking the one in the center gives the middle value. That's the median.
